s1.syndrome_frame: Acute coronary syndrome with recurrent ventricular arrhythmias and evolving left ventricular dysfunction
salient_findings: Canadian Cardiovascular Society Class III angina
Recurrent sustained polymorphic ventricular tachycardia and ventricular fibrillation
Akinesia of all apical segments with severely reduced LVEF of 35%
key_facts: 67-year-old man with hypertension
Dyslipidaemia
Stage 3 chronic kidney disease
Active smoking (35 pack-years)
Family history of ischaemic heart disease
Prior percutaneous coronary interventions (2008, 2017, 2022) for non-ST-elevation myocardial infarction
Exercise stress test induced angina at 50 W without ECG changes
ECG showed normal sinus rhythm, Q waves in lead III, and biphasic T waves in leads III and aVF
Transthoracic echocardiography revealed a left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) of 65% without regional wall-motion abnormalities
Coronary angiography demonstrated patent stents in the circumflex artery, non-significant disease in the left anterior descending artery, and significant ostial right coronary artery stenosis
Developed worsening chest pain after transfer to the intensive care unit
ECG showed ST-segment elevation in leads V1–V3 after worsening chest pain
Second angiogram showed patent stents but subocclusion of the right coronary postero-lateral branch
Required seven external shocks and 15 minutes of cardiopulmonary resuscitation for ventricular arrhythmias

shortlist.label: Takotsubo cardiomyopathy
shortlist.why_kept: Patient developed akinesia of all apical segments, hyperkinesia of the basal segments, and severely reduced LVEF of 35% after intense emotional and physical stress

shortlist.label: Acute myocardial infarction
shortlist.why_kept: Patient presented with worsening chest pain, ST-segment elevation in leads V1–V3, and significant ostial right coronary artery stenosis

shortlist.label: Stent thrombosis
shortlist.why_kept: Patient had prior percutaneous coronary interventions and developed subocclusion of the right coronary postero-lateral branch

shortlist.label: Long QT syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Patient developed QTc prolongation to 500 ms after recurrent ventricular arrhythmias

shortlist.label: Ischemic cardiomyopathy
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has a history of ischemic heart disease, prior myocardial infarctions, and significant coronary artery disease

raw.rationale: The patient's presentation with worsening chest pain, ECG changes, and subsequent development of ventricular arrhythmias, followed by echocardiography showing akinesia of apical segments, hyperkinesia of basal segments, and severely reduced LVEF, is consistent with takotsubo syndrome, especially given the absence of significant coronary artery disease that would explain the extent of left ventricular dysfunction

rejected.label: Acute myocardial infarction
rejected.why: Coronary angiography did not show complete occlusion of a major coronary artery, and the second angiogram showed patent stents but subocclusion of a branch, which was treated, and the echocardiographic findings are not typical for a large myocardial infarction

rejected.label: Stent thrombosis
rejected.why: The patient had patent stents in the circumflex artery and recent intervention in the right coronary artery, with the issue being subocclusion of a branch, not stent thrombosis

rejected.label: Long QT syndrome
rejected.why: The QTc prolongation to 500 ms occurred after the cardiac events, suggesting it may be a consequence rather than the primary cause of the presentation

rejected.label: Ischemic cardiomyopathy
rejected.why: The patient's LVEF was initially normal, and the subsequent reduction in LVEF with specific wall-motion abnormalities is more suggestive of takotsubo cardiomyopathy than a chronic ischemic process
